questions.question_text: The volume of liquid in litres in an industrial vat after $t$ seconds is $V(t) = 2t^3 + 5t^2 + 10$. What is the instantaneous rate of change of volume $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$ at $t = 2\text{ s}$?

options.why: Evaluates the volume $V(2) = 2(8) + 5(4) + 10 = 46$ instead of the derivative.
Differentiates $2t^3$ incorrectly as $6t$ instead of $6t^2$, giving $6(2) + 10(2) + 2 = 34$.
Only evaluates the derivative of the quadratic term $10t$ at $t = 2$.

questions.question_text: The population $P(t)$ of a town $t$ years after 2020 satisfies $P'(5) = -350$. Which statement best interprets this result?

options.text: In 2025, the population is decreasing at an instantaneous rate of $350\text{ people per year}$.
In 2025, the total population is $350\text{ people}$.
options.why: Confuses the derivative rate $P'(5)$ with the total population $P(5)$.

options.text: Between 2020 and 2025, the population decreased by a total of $350\text{ people}$.
options.why: Confuses the instantaneous rate at $t = 5$ with the total change over five years.

options.text: In 2025, the population is increasing at an instantaneous rate of $350\text{ people per year}$.
options.why: Ignores the negative sign, which represents a decrease in population.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{The derivative } P'(5) = -350\text{ gives the instantaneous rate of change in 2025.}$
$\text{The negative sign indicates the population is decreasing by } 350\text{ people per year}.$

questions.question_text: The temperature of a chemical solution during an experiment is $T(t)^{\circ}\text{C}$ at time $t$ minutes. Which mathematical expression represents the question: "At what rate is the temperature changing after $8\text{ minutes}$?"

options.why: Represents the temperature at $t = 8\text{ minutes}$, not the rate of change.
Finds the time when the temperature reaches $8^{\circ}\text{C}$.
Finds the time when the rate of temperature change is $8^{\circ}\text{C/min}$.

questions.solution_text: $\text{The rate of change of temperature after } 8\text{ minutes is given by the derivative evaluated at } t = 8\text{, which is } T'(8).$

questions.question_text: The height in metres of a projectile is given by $h(t) = 50t - 5t^2$, where $t$ is in seconds. At what time is the instantaneous rate of change of height equal to $10\text{ m/s}$?

options.why: Solves for when the projectile reaches maximum height where $h'(t) = 0$.
Solves $h(t) = 0$ for when the projectile returns to the ground.
Arithmetic error in rearranging $50 - 10t = 10$.

questions.question_text: The mass $M$ in grams of crystals forming in a solution after $t$ hours is $M(t) = 15t^2 - t^3$ for $0 \le t \le 10$. What is the rate of crystal formation at $t = 3\text{ hours}$?

options.why: Evaluates the mass $M(3) = 15(9) - 27 = 108$ instead of the derivative.
Calculates $30(3) - 3(3) = 81$ instead of squaring $t$ in $3t^2$.
Differentiates $15t^2 - t^3$ incorrectly as $15t - 3t^2$.

questions.question_text: The mass $m$ in kg of an evaporating block of dry ice after $t$ minutes is $m(t)$. A scientist determines that $m'(12) = -0.45\text{ kg/min}$. What does the value $-0.45$ signify?

options.text: The mass is decreasing at an instantaneous rate of $0.45\text{ kg/min}$ at $t = 12\text{ minutes}$.
The total mass of the dry ice after $12\text{ minutes}$ is $0.45\text{ kg}$.
options.why: Confuses the rate of change $m'(12)$ with the remaining mass $m(12)$.

options.text: The dry ice will completely evaporate in $0.45\text{ minutes}$.
options.why: Misinterprets the rate as the remaining time until total sublimation.

options.text: The mass is increasing at a rate of $0.45\text{ kg/min}$ after $12\text{ minutes}$.
options.why: Ignores the negative sign which indicates mass loss.

questions.solution_text: $\text{The derivative } m'(12) = -0.45\text{ kg/min indicates that after } 12\text{ minutes, the dry ice mass is decreasing at } 0.45\text{ kg/min}.$

questions.question_text: The volume of fuel in a rocket is $F(t)$ litres at $t$ seconds after launch. Which equation corresponds to finding the time when fuel is being consumed at a rate of $120\text{ L/s}$?

options.why: Ignores that fuel consumption represents a decrease in volume, which requires a negative rate of change.
Represents the time when the remaining fuel volume is $120\text{ litres}$.
Evaluates the derivative at $t = 120\text{ seconds}$ rather than solving for time.

questions.solution_text: $\text{Fuel consumption means fuel volume is decreasing, so the rate of change is } F'(t) = -120\text{ L/s}.$

questions.question_text: A manufacturer models its revenue in thousands of dollars by $R(x) = 120x - 3x^2$, where $x$ is the number of units produced (in hundreds). At what production level $x$ is the marginal revenue (instantaneous rate of change of revenue) equal to zero?

options.why: Solves $R(x) = 0$ for the break-even quantity instead of $R'(x) = 0$.
Incorrectly divides $120$ by $12$ instead of $6$.
Halves the intercept $120$ without accounting for the coefficient $6$.
